html:
The Battle of Sardarapat was fought in late May 1918 west of Yerevan, where Armenian troops and volunteers stopped an Ottoman army advancing on Yerevan after Russia left World War I.

With the Russian army gone, Ottoman forces had taken Kars and Alexandropol and were moving toward Yerevan and Etchmiadzin. Armenian soldiers, peasants and refugees of the genocide fought at Sardarapat, Bash Abaran and Karakilisa and forced the Ottomans to halt. On 28 May the Armenian council declared the First Republic of Armenia. Many Armenians believe the battle saved the nation from destruction. A memorial with bell towers and winged bulls was built on the field in 1968. The republic lasted until the Soviet takeover of 1920, and the day is Armenia's Republic Day.
